## Problem

`StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` compares the fetched status against `"in_progress"` (underscore), but `wl show --json` returns `"in-progress"` (hyphen). The guard therefore raises `ClaimError` even when the item is correctly claimed — its own error message reports the contradictory "current status: in-progress".

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'skill'); from shared.status_lifecycle import StatusLifecycle; StatusLifecycle.require_claimed('<an-in-progress-work-item-id>')"
```

Observed: `ClaimError: Work item ... must be in_progress before mutation (current status: in-progress)`.

Expected: returns the `wl show` response without raising for an `in-progress` item.

## Impact

The mandated step-7 guard in the plan skill (and the corresponding guards in implement) fails closed on every correctly claimed item, blocking workflows or forcing ad-hoc bypasses.

## Root cause

`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` `require_claimed()` (`if status != "in_progress":`) and `ensure_claimed()` (`if status == "in_progress":`) both compare against the underscore form. Normalise hyphen/underscore before comparing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `require_claimed()` returns normally for an item whose status is `in-progress`.
2. `require_claimed()` still raises `ClaimError` for `open` and `completed` items.
3. `ensure_claimed()` remains a no-op for `in-progress` items (no redundant `wl update`).
4. Unit tests cover both the hyphen and underscore status spellings.

Discovered-from: SA-0MTYJ4MGO007O22W (references the completed fix SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9).
data.title: StatusLifecycle.require_claimed fails closed on hyphenated 'in-progress' status

# Audit runner: pre-review child with `inherited_pass` bypasses children-stage block and summary claims "all children in in_review/done"

Discovered during the audit of `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — `discovered-from:CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I`.

## Problem Statement
The audit runner can report **"Ready to close: Yes"** for a parent work item that has a **critical, pre-review-stage child** (e.g. an auto-triaged `test-failure` item at `intake_complete`), and the report summary falsely claims *"All children are in in_review or done stage."* This produces a false-positive closure verdict.

## Evidence (reproduction)
- Audited item: `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (Tableau-Card-Engine), audit run 2026-09-20.
- The runner auto-executed the full suite (F3 cache-miss path). The unit vitest stage was **SIGKILLed (exit 137)**.
- The test skill triaged this into `CG-0MUA2UWY7002KUQR` — a **critical `test-failure` bug** created as a **child** of the audited item at `status: open`, `stage: intake_complete`.
- The runner then reported `Ready to close: Yes` with summary: *"All children are in in_review or done stage."*
- The persisted report's `## Children Status` **does** render the child as `CG-0MUA2UWY7002KUQR — open/intake_complete` with verdict `met` ("Inherited from parent pass") — directly contradicting the summary.

## Root Cause
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~9855-9861, `if not parent_gaps:` branch): when the parent passes with no gaps, **every** child gets `cr["inherited_pass"] = True` and `cr["child_audit_ready"] = True` — with **no stage guard**. The only guard is `_child_content_changed`, which is false for a brand-new child.
- `audit_runner.py:4207`: `all_children_reviewed = all(c.get("stage") in ("in_review","done") or c.get("inherited_pass") ...)` — `inherited_pass` exempts a **pre-review** child from the blocking children-stage check.
- `audit_runner.py:4333`: the summary unconditionally appends *"All children are in in_review or done stage."* when `all_children_reviewed` is true, even when a child is actually at `intake_complete`/`idea`/`plan_complete`.

## Expected Behaviour
- A child in a pre-review stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) MUST block parent closure, per the documented rule ("only pre-review stages block") and `SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I`.
- `inherited_pass` (parent-first pass-through, `SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F`) must not exempt a pre-review child from the stage check — at minimum it must not apply to a child created during the audit run (auto-triaged `test-failure`).
- The summary text must be accurate: if any child is not in `in_review`/`done`, say so and produce "Ready to close: No".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1**: A parent with any non-deleted child in `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete` reports "Ready to close: No" and names the blocking child, regardless of `inherited_pass`. → Covered by: SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2 (fix 2: all_children_reviewed check)
- [ ] **AC2**: `inherited_pass` is only applied to children in `in_review`/`done` (or explicitly exempted with a documented rationale), never to pre-review children. → Covered by: SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2 (fix 1: inherited_pass stage guard)
- [ ] **AC3**: The summary's "All children are in in_review or done stage." line is only emitted when that is actually true; otherwise it names the blocking children. → Covered by: SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2 (fix 3: summary text)
- [ ] **AC4**: Regression test: auditing a parent whose child sits at `intake_complete` (with `inherited_pass` otherwise set) yields "Ready to close: No". → Covered by: SA-0MUD5OMQG0068P4I (regression test)

## Child Tasks
- **SA-0MUD5OMQG0068P4I** — Regression test: inherited_pass does not bypass pre-review stage block (test-first)
- **SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2** — Fix: inherited_pass bypasses pre-review stage block (3 fixes in audit_runner.py)

## Secondary observation (may warrant a follow-up item)
- AC5 ("Full project test suite must pass") was marked `met` by the Phase 1 model even though the runner's own suite execution was killed (exit 137). The documented fail-open semantics say execution-dependent ACs should stay `partial` on a red/error run. Confirm whether a red/killed run must force `partial` on execution-dependent ACs.

## Related Work
- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency (child verdict blocks parent regardless of stage) — completed; the inverse problem.
- `SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I` — If a child audit is not ready to close then the parent must also be marked not ready to close — completed.
- `SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F` — parent-first pass-through (`inherited_pass`).

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ~4201-4214 (children-stage check), ~4333 (summary text), ~9855-9861 (`inherited_pass` assignment).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** – [CRITICAL] Audit runner has circular dependency — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage (completed)
- **SA-0MSPPIC4P00849VK** – create_quality_epics.py (code-review + code_review): exact-title LIKE query (completed)
- **SA-0MQNR1I92004Z03R** – IntakeAll error recovery fails on abort, leaving items in completed+idea (contradictory state) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mskb6vja005n43f, ac5, acceptance, acs, actually (+139 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mskb6vja005n43f, ac5, acceptance, acs, actually (+124 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: acceptance, acs, actually, also, appends (+115 more)

# Intake Brief: Misleading completion message on LLM summaries

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report renderer (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) always concludes with "This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}." regardless of whether the skill actually completed successfully — the AC verdict column may show "unmet" but the conclusion line remains positive, creating a misleading impression.

## Users

- **AI agents** running skills — they rely on the report to know whether further action is needed.
- **Producers** reviewing work items — they need clear signals about whether the skill session succeeded or requires re-run.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The conclusion line in `render_report` reflects the actual outcome: use "completed" when all acceptance criteria are met, and "incomplete" (or similar) when any criterion is unmet or a failure occurred.
2. When the outcome is incomplete, the message includes a clear indication of required action (e.g., "requires attention" or "ready for re-run").
3. When the outcome is completed, the message retains the "Ready for {next_action}" phrasing (unchanged behaviour for successful runs).
4. All existing tests in `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` pass after the change.
5. The report header line (`# Completed {skill_name}`) is consistent with the actual outcome — if incomplete, the header should reflect that (e.g., `# Incomplete {skill_name}` or similar).

## Constraints

- Must remain backwards compatible with all callers (library usage and CLI mode).
- The `acceptance_criteria` parameter is already passed to `render_report`; the change must derive status from this without requiring new parameters.
- The change must not alter the structure of the metadata, producer actions, or notes sections.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` in `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` always outputs:
  - Header: `# Completed {skill_name}`
  - Conclusion: `This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}.`
- AC verdicts are passed as `(ac#, description, metric, verdict)` tuples where `verdict` is `"met"` or `"unmet"`.
- `derive_status()` in `shared/herdr_pane` already exists and can determine session status from ACs/producer actions/notes.

## Desired change

- Derive a session status (completed/incomplete) from the `acceptance_criteria` parameter.
- Condition the header and conclusion text on this status.
- For incomplete sessions: surface a clear "incomplete" status and indicate what action is needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Core change: condition header and conclusion on AC verdicts.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Tests for the new conditional behaviour.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — May need to expose a function to derive completion status from ACs for reuse.

## Related work

- **SA-0MM1AWO6D1RVZF3I** — "Define abort behavior and messaging" (blocked) — related theme (abort messaging) but scoped to the cleanup skill specifically; this work addresses the general report renderer.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Backwards compatibility** — Callers relying on the current "Completed" header unchanged when ACs are all met.
- **Empty AC list** — When no ACs are supplied, the renderer currently shows a placeholder row. Assumption: empty AC list + no producer actions + no notes = "completed"; any producer actions or notes = "incomplete".
- **Scope** — Some skills may have inline completion messages outside `render_report`. Scope is limited to `render_report.py`; other files are noted as a potential follow-up.
- **Scope creep** — General messaging improvements across all skills are out of scope; this addresses only the report renderer.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the header (`# Completed {skill_name}`) also change when incomplete, or only the conclusion? — **Answer (agent analysis):** Both should change for consistency. The header should read `# Incomplete {skill_name}` (or similar) when any AC is unmet. Source: design analysis.
- Q: What constitutes "incomplete" — any single unmet AC, or a threshold (e.g., more than 50% unmet)? — **Answer (work item description):** Any unmet AC or failure should be treated as incomplete. The description states "meaning the skill needs to be run again or the producer has an action." Source: work-item description.
- Q: Should producer-actions or notes also influence the status (e.g., notes indicating a known blocker)? — **Answer (agent analysis):** Notes can indicate context but should not override AC verdicts. Producer actions needing attention is an additional signal but AC verdicts are the primary determinant. Source: design analysis.
data.title: Misleading completion message on LLM summaries

# Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done

**Recurring defect — producer has raised this repeatedly.** Policy restated by the producer (2026-10-02): *if a parent is marked `completed` and it has been audited, then all its children are considered complete.* The concrete fix requested: **when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `status=completed, stage=done`.**

## Problem statement

When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent work item, its descendants are left in whatever terminal or non-terminal state they previously held. This lets a parent reach `status=completed, stage=in_review` with a passing audit while its children remain `open`/`blocked`/`in_progress` (or already `done`), so downstream steps can neither treat the subtree as consistent nor close the parent without a manual `wl close --force` sweep.

## Users and user stories

- **Primary user — release producer.** As a producer, when I audit a parent work item and the audit passes, I want every descendant to be marked `completed`/`done` automatically so that I never have to force-close the parent and sweep unfinished children as a side effect.
- **Secondary user — the ship pipeline (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`).** As the post-release close step, I want an audit-approved parent's descendants to already be terminal so the collateral-descendant guard does not falsely refuse to close released items.
- **Secondary user — audit operators/agents.** As an audit operator, I want the cascade to be idempotent and authorised only by a passing parent audit, so reruns and failed audits never resurrect or mutate work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cascade on passing parent audit.** When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent item (`readyToClose === true`, i.e. `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` on the success path), every descendant is set to `status=completed, stage=done`, and each cascaded child receives an explanatory comment naming the authorising parent and the audit timestamp.
- [ ] **AC2 — Idempotent and `deleted`-safe.** Re-running the cascade on an already-terminal tree produces no further mutations or duplicate comments; `deleted` descendants are skipped; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cascade without a passing audit.** A parent audit that fails (`Ready to close: No`), is fallback-tainted, or has not been run performs **no** cascade and leaves descendants untouched. Cascading is authorised by a passing audit verdict only — never by status/stage alone.
- [ ] **AC4 — Ship close step closes the parent without a refusal.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` closes a parent whose descendants are all terminal (`done`/`deleted`) without a refusal, covered by unit tests that inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` (overlaps SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP tasks).
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests cover the behaviour.** Passing-parent → children done (with comments); failing-parent → children untouched; parent with a mix of `deleted`/`done`/`open` children → only the appropriate action; cascade rerun → no further mutation (testing/validation criterion).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing audit and ship suites pass.** The existing audit runner and ship suites pass and `npm run build` passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` as applicable).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The cascade must live where the verdict is known — the parent audit success path in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — not only as a special case inside the ship close step.
- Any `wl` mutations must respect the `StatusLifecycle` claim invariant (an item must be `in_progress` before mutation) and route `--worklog-dir` through the shared resolution helpers so the cascade targets the item's own worklog store regardless of cwd.
- The cascade must not weaken the existing scope guard (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H): a parent whose audit has **not** passed must still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants.
- Must remain safe under dry-run (`--do-not-persist`): a dry-run passing verdict must not mutate descendants.

## Existing state

- **Verdict knowledge.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` computes the parent verdict at `audit_verdict = _parse_ready_to_close(report)` (~line 11363) and, in the terminal transition block, takes the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch (~line 11773) to run `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (or `--stage done` when already done). This is the natural single point to trigger the cascade.
- **Child-state checks today.** `_check_children_stages` / related helpers already classify children in `in_review`/`done` as exempt but do **not** mutate them; `inherited_pass` records a verdict reuse but never sets `completed`/`done`.
- **Ship close step.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (~line 370) computes `candidateIds` from `getCandidateItems()` (= `stage=in_review` only) and refuses a `--force` close when `collateral = descendants.filter(id => !candidateIds.has(id))` is non-empty (~line 534). Descendants already `stage=done` therefore always appear as collateral — tracked narrowly as SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP.
- **Evidence (TCE v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02).** Five parents sat at `completed/in_review` after the release, all audit-approved; the close step refused all five (25 open/blocked children on two of them), and all five had to be closed with `wl close --force`, sweeping 50 descendants to `done`.

## Desired change

1. Add a cascade helper (e.g. `_cascade_descendants_terminal`) in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` that, given a parent id and audit timestamp, walks descendants (`wl show <id> --children` recursively or the existing tree helpers), skips `deleted` and already `completed`/`done` items, and for each remaining descendant issues `wl update <child> --status completed --stage done`, followed by `wl comment add <child>` with a reason naming the parent and audit timestamp.
2. Invoke the helper from the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success branch only (and not on the failure/fallback restore branches), after the parent's own verified transition succeeds; suppress it under dry-run.
3. Make the helper idempotent (no mutation/comment when a child is already terminal) and non-fatal (a cascade failure for one child is logged and does not abort the audit, matching the ship step's non-blocking semantics).
4. Keep `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`'s collateral logic unchanged apart from SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP's `done`/`deleted` exclusion (defence-in-depth).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Add the cascade helper and call it on the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success path; reuse existing descendant/`_run_wl` helpers.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Ensure `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` excludes terminal (`done`/`deleted`) descendants from `collateral` (SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP); add/verify injected-fn unit coverage for AC4.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — New cascade regression tests (passing parent, failing parent, mixed child states, idempotent rerun, dry-run).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — Extend lifecycle-transition tests to assert cascade/no-cascade per verdict.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — Unit tests for the terminal-descendant non-refusal (AC4).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` — Document cascade-on-audit behaviour (AC7).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** (open) — "Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`": the narrower ship-side workaround. This item is the root-cause counterpart; they should be implemented together (or this item's AC1–AC3 makes the ship-side workaround unnecessary, keeping SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP as defence-in-depth).
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (in-progress) — "Audit runner: pre-review child with `inherited_pass` bypasses children-stage block and summary claims all children in `in_review`/`done`": the likely mechanism by which parents reach `in_review` with open children; fixing it prevents the "unfinished children under a done parent" failure mode.
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** (completed) — "wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK": the original decision; cascade-on-audit is the missing enforcement.
- **SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA** (completed) — "Parent audit should pass when all children's ACs are met".
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** (completed) — "Audit: parent-first child pass-through".
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** (completed) — the scope guard that must not regress.
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** (completed) — "Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits" (automated find-related match).
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** (completed) — "Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable" (automated find-related match).
- **Provenance:** filed from the Tableau-Card-Engine v0.1.19 release retro (2026-10-02).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — scope creep into the ship step.** The root fix is audit-side; touching `run-release.js` beyond the terminal-descendant exclusion risks duplicating SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP. Mitigation: keep the ship change minimal and additive.
- **Risk — partial cascade on `wl` failure.** A mid-cascade `wl` failure could leave a subtree half-terminal. Mitigation: per-child try/except, loud logging, idempotent rerun, non-fatal semantics; the next audit success completes the cascade.
- **Risk — comment noise / non-idempotence.** Re-auditing a passing parent must not duplicate comments. Mitigation: skip already-terminal children before commenting; test the rerun path (AC2/AC5).
- **Risk — regression to the audit scope guard.** Cascading on a *failed* verdict would bypass SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H. Mitigation: cascade only on the `audit_verdict == "yes"` branch; explicit failing-parent test (AC3/AC5).
- **Assumption.** "Descendants" means the full recursive subtree of the audited parent (children, grandchildren, …), consistent with `wl close --force`'s recursive sweep.
- **Assumption.** A passing parent audit is the sole authorisation signal; `status`/`stage` alone never authorises a cascade.
- **Assumption.** `deleted` descendants are historical and must never be re-marked or commented on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Are any clarifications required beyond the seed context? — **Answer (producer, via the filed work item SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP and the TCE v0.1.19 release retro, 2026-10-02):** No. The seed context specifies the policy, the concrete requested fix ("when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `completed`/`done`"), the desired behaviour (5 points), the acceptance criteria, and the related work. The interview was therefore skipped per the intake "seed context suffices" rule.
- **Q:** Where should the cascade live? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §2):** In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` on the parent audit success path — a single source of truth where the verdict is known — not only as a special case in the ship close step. Evidence: repository inspection confirms the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` branch (~`audit_runner.py:11773`) is the success transition point.
- **Q:** How should `deleted` and already-terminal descendants be treated? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §3):** `deleted` children are left untouched; reruns are no-ops; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
data.title: Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done
